architecture.mechanism: Dynamic, model-directed allocation of coolant among parallel branches: a first-principles coolant model coupled with valve-actuation models predicts each branch's thermal/flow response, so commanded allocation can be compared against measured response to localize a flow-path anomaly.
architecture.intervention: Add (or reuse) shut-off/bypass valves to sequentially command coolant flow to individual engine-cooling branches—driver-side heater core, radiator, engine block, heater bypass—while logging branch inlet/outlet temperature, flow, and system pressure, and compare each transient against a first-principles model of the circuit, mirroring the paper's closed-loop comparison of predicted vs. actual thermal response.
architecture.expected_effect: The seeping branch shows a model-prediction mismatch (missing flow, lagging temperature rise, or pressure decay) with no visible drip, localizing the leak—most plausibly the driver-side heater core or its connections, matching the stronger driver-side coolant smell.
architecture.falsification_test: Warm and pressurize the system, command flow only to the heater-core branch, and hold; if the model's predicted outlet-temperature rise and pressure hold are not met (outlet lags, pressure decays), the leak is in that branch—confirm by dye/borescope after isolation; if every branch matches model predictions within tolerance, the mechanism is falsified and the source is external seepage evaporating on a hot surface.
